title: Green Chilli
subtitle: New Mexican slow-braised pork and green chilli stew
excerpt: Pork shoulder slow-braised with roasted green chillies, garlic, and stock until the pork is falling apart and the sauce is thick, fragrant, and intensely savoury. The New Mexico version: no tomatoes, no beans, no cumin. Just pork, chilli, and time.

recipe.sourceNotes: Green chilli stew is the signature dish of New Mexico and southern Colorado, distinct from Tex-Mex chilli con carne in almost every respect. It uses fresh or roasted green chillies rather than dried red ones, pork rather than beef, and contains neither beans nor tomatoes. The Hatch Valley in New Mexico grows the most prized chillies for this dish: Hatch green chillies, harvested in late summer and roasted over wood fires. Outside New Mexico, Anaheim or poblano chillies are the closest substitutes. The dish is served as a sauce over eggs, smothered burritos, or eaten plain with flour tortillas. The only essential technique is slow braising; the pork must cook until the collagen melts and the meat shreds in the sauce.

content.text: Roast the chillies directly over a gas flame or under a very hot grill until charred all over, then steam in a plastic bag for 10 minutes before peeling and seeding. This concentrates the flavour and removes the tough skin. The stew can be made a day ahead; it improves overnight.

items.preparation: boneless shoulder preferred; cut into 3 cm chunks
green chillies such as Anaheim or poblano; roasted, peeled, seeded, and chopped

content.text: Season the pork. Heat the oil in a large, heavy pot over high heat and brown the pork in batches until deeply coloured on all sides. Transfer to a plate.

Add the onion to the pot and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano. Cook for 1 minute. Return the pork. Add the chopped roasted chillies and pour in the stock. Bring to a simmer.

Cover and braise on the lowest possible heat for 2.5 to 3 hours until the pork is completely tender and beginning to break apart. Remove the lid for the last 30 minutes to reduce the liquid to a thick sauce. Taste and adjust salt. Serve over rice, eggs, or with warm flour tortillas.
